headline: Infineon retargets IEEE P1687.2 test descriptions into SystemVerilog UVM for automotive smart-power shift-left
fact: An Infineon Automotive Power paper at ETS 2026 describes retargeting IJTAG/IEEE P1687.2 test-case descriptions through a renderer and a pin-level time-stamp/value transport such as STIL into top-level SystemVerilog UVM testbenches for pre-silicon functional verification of automotive smart-power devices. Its SoC DUT combines digital RTL with analog behavioral models, while UVM-compatible agents apply external analog and supply stimuli. The paper illustrates replay of a measured noisy supply waveform and shows a charge-pump voltage (VDD CP) response to supply interruptions followed by an SPI diagnostic readout. These are paper-reported verification results, not measured silicon performance or evidence of wider adoption.

sources.title: Shift-Left by applying IEEE P1687.2 to SystemVerilog test-benches for Automotive Smart-Power devices
sources.summary: Infineon Automotive Power paper: Section III describes digital RTL enriched by analog behavioral models and external analog/supply stimuli applied by UVM-compatible agents; Section II B/Figures 5–6 illustrates noisy-supply waveform replay, and Section V/Figure 8 shows the charge-pump voltage response to supply interruptions followed by an SPI diagnostic readout in the pre-silicon testbench.
